summary.title: A bot for Starcraft in Rust, C or any other language
summary.one_liner: You learn how BWAPI-C wraps the C++ StarCraft: Brood War bot API in a C interface, and how to build a Rust bot on top of it with FFI and bindgen.
keywords: write a starcraft bot in rust
wrap c++ library with c api
cross compile windows dll from linux
takeaways: Rust can call C libraries via FFI, and rust-bindgen can generate the declarations from C headers automatically.
BWAPI is C++ and bindgen cannot handle it directly, so the author wrapped it in a C API (BWAPI-C) using extern "C" and opaque pointers.
A StarCraft bot is a DLL exporting newAIModule and gameInit, with event handlers that get called on game events.
The Rust layer is split into a -sys crate (raw bindings) and a high-level crate (bwapi-rs) with newtype wrappers and idiomatic types.
A known unsolved issue: the bindings cannot guarantee unique references, so &mut and & aliasing can cause undefined behavior.
summary.summary: The article describes building a StarCraft: Brood War bot framework. The author explains BWAPI, a C++ API, and why bindgen fails on it, so they wrote BWAPI-C, a C wrapper using extern "C" and opaque pointers. It then shows how to write a bot DLL in C and in Rust, using a -sys crate generated by bindgen plus a high-level bwapi-rs layer that implements an event handler trait. The piece ends by noting the OpenBW open-source alternative and an unresolved aliasing problem in the Rust bindings.
